Context: what polemics is and why the Ch.back: From Greek **pólemos, "war"**: the examination and refutation of teachings opposed to the faith. The war is against error, not people (Ephesians 6:12).

Context: what polemics is and why the Ch.front: Why does the Orthodox Church answer other faiths at all?
Context: what polemics is and why the Ch.back: **For the truth** (Christ is the truth), **for the faithful** (so they are not drawn away), and **for the other person** (a good answer is an invitation).

Context: what polemics is and why the Ch.front: How does polemics differ from the History and Philosophy curriculums?
Context: what polemics is and why the Ch.back: Those keep the rule of **not arriving at a position**. Polemics **arrives**, but first gives each position at its strongest, in its own words.

Apologia and polemic: giving an answer f.back: A **defence**, as in court: "be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear" (KJV).

Apologia and polemic: giving an answer f.front: Apologetics and polemics: what is the difference?
Apologia and polemic: giving an answer f.back: **Apologetics** answers "why do you believe?" and defends the faith; **polemics** answers "why not believe this instead?" and examines the other position. Both are needed.

Apologia and polemic: giving an answer f.front: What four conditions does 1 Peter 3:15 set on an answer?
Apologia and polemic: giving an answer f.back: Begin in **prayer** ("sanctify the Lord God in your hearts"); **prepare** ("be ready always"); answer the **question asked**; and answer with **meekness and fear**.

Heresy, schism and heterodoxy: the words.back: "Choice", then "party": **choosing one's own opinion over the faith received**, on a matter of the faith itself, and holding to it after correction (Titus 3:10).

Heresy, schism and heterodoxy: the words.front: St Basil's Letter 188 (374): heresy, schism, unlawful congregation
Heresy, schism and heterodoxy: the words.back: **Heresy**: broken off in the faith itself. **Schism**: separated over church questions "capable of mutual solution". **Parasynagogē**: a rival assembly under disorderly clergy.
"Other belief", the opposite of orthodoxy. The **gentler, general word** for Christians outside the Orthodox Church, not settling in every case whether it is heresy strictly.

\"There must be also heresies\": why err.back: "Approved", like **metal that has passed the assay**: "there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest".

\"There must be also heresies\": why err.front: How does a heresy usually arise, according to the Fathers?
\"There must be also heresies\": why err.back: It takes **one true thing and makes it the whole**, cutting it loose from the rest of the faith (Arius from God's oneness; Nestorius from Christ's humanity).
Greek *kanōn tēs alētheias*: the **summary of the faith taught to every baptised person**, later fixed in the Creed; the test of any teaching.

Speaking the truth in love: why truth an.back: "**Speaking the truth in love**": one Greek verb, "truthing", done in love. Not truth softened, nor love that drops truth, but truth given as love.

Speaking the truth in love: why truth an.front: What are the two failures that Ephesians 4:15 rules out?
Speaking the truth in love: why truth an.back: **Truth without love**: contempt, mockery, point-scoring. **Love without truth**: "all paths are the same", indifference wearing a kind face.

Speaking the truth in love: why truth an.front: What does love require of a person arguing for the faith?
Speaking the truth in love: why truth an.back: **Understand before answering; never misrepresent; admit your own side's wrongs; want the other's good, not your victory.**

Reading: St Paul at the Areopagus (Acts.back: The Athenian council that judged new teachings, where **St Paul spoke in Acts 17**; he began from the altar "TO THE UNKNOWN GOD".
A line from **Aratus**, a Stoic poet of the 3rd century BC, which Paul quotes to the Athenians; "in him we live" is often traced to Epimenides.

Reading: St Paul at the Areopagus (Acts.front: At what point did Paul's Athenian hearers mock, and what does it teach?
Reading: St Paul at the Areopagus (Acts.back: At **the resurrection of the dead** (17:32). He did not drop it to keep them listening: **common ground is a door, not a room to stay in.**

The Areopagus method: common ground with.front: What are the four moves of the Areopagus method?
The Areopagus method: common ground with.back: **Acknowledge** what is good, **connect** it to what it points toward, **correct** where it contradicts itself, **proclaim** what only Christ gives.

The Areopagus method: common ground with.front: Why can the Christian recognise truth in other faiths without fear?
The Areopagus method: common ground with.back: Because Christ is the **Logos through whom all things were made** (John 1:3): whatever is true anywhere comes from Him, and its fullness is in Him.

The Areopagus method: common ground with.front: The wall and the bridge to nowhere: what are the two errors?
The Areopagus method: common ground with.back: **The wall**: treating the other faith as wholly false. **The bridge to nowhere**: treating common ground as the whole, so the Gospel becomes what everyone already believes.

St Justin Martyr: the seeds of the Word.back: Born in Samaria; Christian philosopher in Rome; *First Apology* (about 155), *Dialogue with Trypho* (about 160); **beheaded in Rome about 165**. Feast 1 June.
"The **seed-bearing Word**" (Justin, *Second Apology* 13): the philosophers "spoke well in proportion to the share" they had of it. Seeds, not the whole.

St Justin Martyr: the seeds of the Word.front: What does Justin mean by "whatever things were rightly said among all men, are the property of us Christians"?
St Justin Martyr: the seeds of the Word.back: Truth anywhere comes from the Word, so it **belongs to Christ**; but the seed "is one thing, and quite another is the thing itself".

Reading: St Irenaeus on error dressed as.back: Five books against **the Gnostics** by Irenaeus, bishop of Lyons (about 130–202), who had heard St Polycarp. Book I describes; Books II–V refute.

Reading: St Irenaeus on error dressed as.front: What does Irenaeus's image of the glass and the emerald teach?
Reading: St Irenaeus on error dressed as.back: A clever fake fools all but "one able to test". **The answer to counterfeit is knowing the real jewel well**, which is why polemics depends on theology.

Reading: St Irenaeus on error dressed as.front: Why does Irenaeus say error is dangerous?
Reading: St Irenaeus on error dressed as.back: Because it is **"craftily decked out in an attractive dress"**, made to seem "more true than the truth itself", and its language resembles ours while its meaning differs.

St Irenaeus's answer: the rule of faith.front: How did Irenaeus answer the Gnostics' claim to a secret tradition?
St Irenaeus's answer: the rule of faith.back: With **the rule of faith** held by every church alike, and **the public succession of bishops**: the apostles would have given any secret to those they appointed.

St Irenaeus's answer: the rule of faith.front: Irenaeus's mosaic of the king (Against Heresies I.8.1)
St Irenaeus's answer: the rule of faith.back: Heretics take Scripture's jewels and **rearrange the king's portrait into a dog or a fox**, then claim it is still the king.
"Every Church should agree with this Church, on account of its **preeminent authority**." Catholics read universal authority; Orthodox read Rome's witness in that age.

St Athanasius: answering the pagans and.back: Bishop of Alexandria from **328**; at Nicaea as a deacon; **exiled five times**. Feasts 18 January and 2 May.

St Athanasius: answering the pagans and.front: Against the Heathen and On the Incarnation
St Athanasius: answering the pagans and.back: Athanasius's **two-book work** against paganism: the soul invented idols by turning from God; the Word became man to restore God's image and destroy death.

St Athanasius: answering the pagans and.front: How did Athanasius argue against Arius?
St Athanasius: answering the pagans and.back: **From salvation**: only God can unite us to God, so a created Son cannot save. **From worship**: the Church has always worshipped Christ.

St John of Damascus: On Heresies and the.front: The Fount of Knowledge (St John of Damascus)
St John of Damascus: On Heresies and the.back: Three parts: **Philosophical Chapters**, **On Heresies** (about a hundred), and **An Exact Exposition of the Orthodox Faith**. Tools, then errors, then the truth.
The "**medicine chest**" describing **eighty heresies** with their antidotes; the main source of St John of Damascus's *On Heresies*.

St John of Damascus: On Heresies and the.front: What does this curriculum add to St John of Damascus's map of heresies?
St John of Damascus: On Heresies and the.back: **The other side's case at its strongest, from its own texts**, which his short entries, sometimes from hostile sources, usually lack.

The method of this curriculum: four step.front: What are the four steps of this curriculum's method?
The method of this curriculum: four step.back: 1. **Their case at its strongest**, from their own texts. 2. **The Orthodox answer**, saying which source. 3. **Their best reply**. 4. **What it finally rests on.**

The method of this curriculum: four step.front: What is the test of step 1, their case at its strongest?
The method of this curriculum: four step.back: Would **their best defender** read it and say "**yes, that is what we believe**"? Never learn a position from an exposé.

The method of this curriculum: four step.front: Why must the Orthodox answer name its source?
The method of this curriculum: four step.back: Because a **council's definition is not the same as one writer's opinion**; the answerer must know how much weight his answer carries.

The fallacies that sink an argument.back: **Straw man**: attacking a weaker version than the one held. **Steelman**: stating the other position at its strongest before answering.
Using one word in two senses: **"grace", "church", "tradition", "saved"** mean different things to each side. Define terms first.

The fallacies that sink an argument.front: Which fallacies tempt the Orthodox answerer in particular?
The fallacies that sink an argument.back: **Tu quoque** (meeting every charge with a Western sin), **the genetic fallacy** ("it is Western, so it is wrong"), and **citing a saint's opinion as if it were a council**.

Scripture as common ground: why both sid.front: Why can a disagreement between Christians not be settled by verses alone?
Scripture as common ground: why both sid.back: Because the verses must be fitted together by a **framework**: Tradition, a confession, or private judgement. **The disagreement usually lives in the framework.**

Scripture as common ground: why both sid.front: What three layers does an answer to another Christian usually have?
Scripture as common ground: why both sid.back: **The text** (what the verse says), **the reading** (how the Church read it before the dispute), **the framework** (why read it that way).

Scripture as common ground: why both sid.front: What common ground should be used with Jews, Muslims and atheists?
Scripture as common ground: why both sid.back: With **Jews**, the Old Testament; with **Muslims**, the Qur'an (which says the earlier books were changed); with **atheists**, evidence and reason. **Use what they accept.**

Akriveia and oikonomia: strictness and m.front: "For the sake of management of the majority" (St Basil, Letter 188)
Akriveia and oikonomia: strictness and m.back: *Oikonomias heneka tōn pollōn*: Basil states the strict view of the Cathari's baptism, then allows it **to be accepted for the sake of the many**.

Akriveia and oikonomia: strictness and m.front: What do Orthodox writers agree about oikonomia?
Akriveia and oikonomia: strictness and m.back: It **never changes doctrine**, only practice; it is exercised **by the Church through her bishops**; and it **serves salvation**.

Akriveia and oikonomia: strictness and m.front: What does the disagreement over oikonomia and heterodox sacraments rest on?
Akriveia and oikonomia: strictness and m.back: Whether **grace is bound to the Church's canonical boundaries** (St Nikodemos, the *Pedalion*) or **reaches beyond them in some measure** (Florovsky, "The Limits of the Church", 1933).

How the Church receives converts: baptis.front: Canon 95 of the Council in Trullo (692)
How the Church receives converts: baptis.back: Repeats canon 7 of Constantinople I: some heretics are received by **written renunciation and chrismation**, others (Eunomians, Montanists, Sabellians) **"as heathen", by baptism**.
Signed with the patriarchs of Alexandria and Jerusalem; required that **Latins and Protestants be baptised** on entering the Orthodox Church.

How the Church receives converts: baptis.front: What does the disagreement over baptising converts rest on?
How the Church receives converts: baptis.back: Whether a Trinitarian baptism outside the Church is **empty until the Church fills it** (so baptise, for certainty) or **real though incomplete** (so chrismate, as canon 95 and long practice do).

Looking back: how the Church answers.front: Which five models of answering does Polemics Stage 1 draw from?
Looking back: how the Church answers.back: **St Paul at Athens, St Justin, St Irenaeus, St Athanasius, St John of Damascus.**

Looking back: how the Church answers.front: What may be hoped for those outside the Church, in Orthodox writers?
Looking back: how the Church answers.back: Undefined. One side: **the Church alone is the ark of salvation**, presume nothing. The other: **God is not bound by His sacraments**. Both: proclaim, and leave judgement to God.

Context: why the old heresies keep comin.front: Why do the same heresies keep returning, according to Polemics Stage 2?
Context: why the old heresies keep comin.back: The Gospel's claims (one God in three, Christ God and man, God in matter) can be "simplified" in **only a few ways**, so the same errors recur.

Context: why the old heresies keep comin.front: Name the six ancient heresies of Polemics Stage 2 and their modern echoes.
Context: why the old heresies keep comin.back: **Gnosticism** (lost gospels), **Marcion** (Old Testament set aside), **Arius** (Witnesses), **modalism** (Oneness Pentecostals), **Nestorius** (refusing Theotokos), **iconoclasm** (Reformed objection to images).

Context: why the old heresies keep comin.front: Why are the Oriental Orthodox not answered in Polemics Stage 2?
Context: why the old heresies keep comin.back: They are **not heirs of these heresies**; Theology Stages 7 and 12 teach them as the churches that did not receive Chalcedon, with the dialogues.

Gnosticism: secret knowledge and an evil.back: "**Knowledge**": 2nd-century movements (Valentinus, Basilides) teaching salvation by **secret knowledge** that frees the divine spark from matter.
"**Craftsman**": the ignorant lesser god who made the material world, sometimes identified with the God of the Old Testament.

Gnosticism: secret knowledge and an evil.front: Docetism, the Gnostic Christ who only seemed to have a body
Gnosticism: secret knowledge and an evil.back: From *dokein*, "to seem": the teaching that **Christ only seemed to have a body**. Answered by 1 John 4:3: Jesus Christ "is come in the flesh".

Gnosticism: secret knowledge and an evil.front: What does the disagreement with Gnosticism finally rest on?
Gnosticism: secret knowledge and an evil.back: **Is the material world the good work of the one God** (Genesis 1:31), **or the botched work of a lesser one?**

Gnosticism today: the lost gospels and t.back: **Thirteen Coptic codices** found in Upper Egypt, copied in the 4th century; over fifty texts, many Gnostic, including the *Gospel of Thomas*.

Gnosticism today: the lost gospels and t.front: How does the Church answer the claim that the Gnostic gospels are as authentic as the four?
Gnosticism today: the lost gospels and t.back: **Dates** (the four are 1st-century, the Gnostic texts mostly 2nd–3rd); **diversity is not equality**; the question is who kept **what the apostles taught publicly**.

Gnosticism today: the lost gospels and t.front: What is the everyday modern form of Gnosticism?
Gnosticism today: the lost gospels and t.back: **"Spiritual but not religious"**: a private inner path, freed from body, Church and sacraments, known to the awakened few.

Marcion: two gods and a shortened Bible.back: Shipowner from Pontus who set the **just God of the Old Testament** against the **good Father of Jesus**; wrote the *Antitheses*.
**One Gospel** (a shortened Luke) and **ten letters of Paul**, edited; the whole Old Testament rejected. The first canon, made by subtraction.

Marcion: two gods and a shortened Bible.front: How did the Fathers answer Marcion's two gods?
Marcion: two gods and a shortened Bible.back: **One God in both Testaments**: Jesus calls Israel's God His Father and said "I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil"; mercy is in the Old, judgement in the New.

Marcion today: the angry God of the Old.back: German historian who argued, in substance, that keeping the Old Testament as canonical in modern Protestantism was the result of **religious and ecclesiastical paralysis**.

Marcion today: the angry God of the Old.front: How do the Fathers read the violent passages of the Old Testament?
Marcion today: the angry God of the Old.back: **In Christ**: some (Origen, Gregory of Nyssa) **spiritually**, as war on the passions; others literally, as **just judgements for a time, not a pattern** for Christians.

Marcion today: the angry God of the Old.front: What does the modern Marcionite question rest on?
Marcion today: the angry God of the Old.back: **Is the Old Testament a record of a different God, or of the same God preparing a people for Christ?**

Arius: the Son as the first and greatest.back: Alexandrian presbyter, pupil of **Lucian of Antioch**; taught from about 318 that **"there was once when the Son was not"**; wrote the *Thalia*.
"**Of one essence with the Father**": the Son is begotten of the Father's essence, **not made**.

Arius: the Son as the first and greatest.front: What does the disagreement with Arius finally rest on?
Arius: the Son as the first and greatest.back: **Is there any being between God and creation?** Arius: the Son is the first creature. Nicaea: the Son is on God's side; there is no third category.

Reading: Arius's letter to Eusebius of N.front: Arius's letter to Eusebius of Nicomedia (about 318)
Reading: Arius's letter to Eusebius of N.back: Preserved in **Theodoret, Ecclesiastical History I**: "before He was begotten, or created, or purposed, or established, He was not."

Reading: Arius's letter to Eusebius of N.front: Which equation does Arius's letter turn on?
Reading: Arius's letter to Eusebius of N.back: He treats **"begotten" and "created" as meaning the same**, so a begotten Son must have a beginning.

Reading: Arius's letter to Eusebius of N.front: Why did Arius's teaching seem pious to many?
Reading: Arius's letter to Eusebius of N.back: It held a **very high view of the Son** ("perfect God, only begotten and unchangeable") while seeming to **protect God's oneness**.

Reading: St Athanasius against \"there w.front: Athanasius's fountain argument (Discourse I against the Arians, §19)
Reading: St Athanasius against \"there w.back: "Once the Son was not" is like saying **"Once the Fountain was dry"**: a fountain that begets nothing is no fountain.

Reading: St Athanasius against \"there w.front: How does Athanasius distinguish begetting from making?
Reading: St Athanasius against \"there w.back: **To beget is to give one's own nature** (a man begets a man); **to make is to produce something else** (a man makes a house). The Son is begotten, so He is what the Father is.

Reading: St Athanasius against \"there w.front: Why is "Father" an eternal name, according to Athanasius?
Reading: St Athanasius against \"there w.back: Because **God is Father by having the Son**; if the Son had a beginning, God's fatherhood would be something that happened to Him.

Arius today: Witnesses, Unitarians and \.front: "The Word was a god" (New World Translation, John 1:1)
Arius today: Witnesses, Unitarians and \.back: The Jehovah's Witnesses' rendering, from the lack of an article before *theos*. Answered: a pre-verbal predicate noun **gives the nature**, "the Word was God".
Means **pre-eminence** as well as order (David made God's "firstborn", Psalm 89:27); verse 16 says all things were created **by Him**.

Arius today: Witnesses, Unitarians and \.front: What do Jehovah's Witnesses hold about the Son?
Arius today: Witnesses, Unitarians and \.back: That He is **Jehovah's first creation**, the archangel **Michael** before His earthly birth, through whom God made everything else.

The modalists: Sabellius and the one God.back: Gave modalism its classic form: **Father, Son and Spirit as one person in three roles**; excommunicated by Pope Callistus about 220.
"**The Father suffered**": the consequence of modalism. Tertullian on Praxeas: "he put to flight the Paraclete, and he crucified the Father."

The modalists: Sabellius and the one God.front: How do the Fathers answer modalism from the Gospels?
The modalists: Sabellius and the one God.back: **The three speak to one another**: the Son prays to the Father and shares glory with Him "before the world was" (John 17:5); "one" in John 10:30 is neuter, *hen*.

Modalism today: Oneness Pentecostals and.back: From a camp meeting at **Arroyo Seco** (1913); hold one God revealed as Father, Son and Spirit, **Jesus the one name**, baptism "in the name of Jesus"; UPCI formed 1945.

Modalism today: Oneness Pentecostals and.front: Why is "water, ice and steam" a bad analogy for the Trinity?
Modalism today: Oneness Pentecostals and.back: It shows **one substance in three successive states**: that is **modalism**, not three persons existing at once.

Modalism today: Oneness Pentecostals and.front: How does the Church answer the Oneness reading of "in the name of Jesus" (Acts 2:38)?
Modalism today: Oneness Pentecostals and.back: It means **by His authority and into Him**; the *Didache* already baptises **in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit**.

Nestorius: two sons and the Theotokos.back: "**She who gave birth to God**": confirmed at **Ephesus (431)** against Nestorius, who preferred *Christotokos*.
Antiochene monk who refused "Theotokos" to keep Christ's natures distinct; deposed at **Ephesus (431)**; died in exile in Egypt about 451.

Nestorius: two sons and the Theotokos.front: Why is the title Theotokos a statement about Christ?
Nestorius: two sons and the Theotokos.back: **Mothers bear persons, not natures**: the person born of Mary is the eternal Word, so she is truly Mother of God.

Nestorius's pattern today: \"the mother.back: Signed by **John Paul II and Mar Dinkha IV** of the Assyrian Church of the East: both confess the same faith in Christ, each keeping its own titles for Mary.

Nestorius's pattern today: \"the mother.front: Why does refusing the title "Mother of God" lead back to Nestorius?
Nestorius's pattern today: \"the mother.back: If Mary bore only the human nature, either the person has no mother or there are **two subjects**; either way **the one who died is not the Word**.

Nestorius's pattern today: \"the mother.front: Is the Church of the East simply Nestorian?
Nestorius's pattern today: \"the mother.back: **No**: its Christology developed in Syriac in its own way and it confesses one Christ; the label is rejected by the church and many scholars.

The iconoclasts: image and idol.front: Council of Hieria (754) and its Christological dilemma
The iconoclasts: image and idol.back: The **iconoclast council** that condemned images, arguing that an icon of Christ either depicts His divinity or **separates His humanity**.

The iconoclasts: image and idol.front: Nicaea II (787) on latreia and proskynesis
The iconoclasts: image and idol.back: **Latreia**, worship, belongs to God alone; **proskynesis**, reverence, is given to icons: "the honour which is paid to the image passes on to that which the image represents".

The iconoclasts: image and idol.front: St John of Damascus, On Holy Images (about 730)
The iconoclasts: image and idol.back: "I do not worship matter, I worship **the God of matter, who became matter for my sake**."

The iconoclasts: image and idol.front: How did the Orthodox answer the iconoclasts' Christological dilemma?
The iconoclasts: image and idol.back: **An icon depicts a person, not a nature**: the Word as He was seen in the flesh, neither depicting the divine nature nor separating it.

Iconoclasm today: the Reformed case agai.back: Calvin allows painting as a gift of God but holds it **"unlawful to give a visible shape to God"**, and more unlawful to worship God in an image.
Lists among sins against the second commandment **"the making any representation of God, of all or of any of the three persons"**.

Iconoclasm today: the Reformed case agai.front: What does the disagreement over icons with the Reformed rest on?
Iconoclasm today: the Reformed case agai.back: **Has the Incarnation changed how the second commandment applies, because God has now been seen?** Orthodox say yes; Reformed say no.

Looking back: the pattern of the old her.front: What is the common shape of every heresy in Polemics Stage 2?
Looking back: the pattern of the old her.back: **A truth cut loose from the rest of the faith**; so the answer grants the truth freely and shows the whole of which it is a part.

Looking back: the pattern of the old her.front: What are the two great lines on which the old heresies fall?
Looking back: the pattern of the old her.back: **The Trinity line** (Arius, modalism) and **the Incarnation line** (Gnosticism, Nestorius, iconoclasm; Marcion in another way).

Context: why Judaism is answered differe.front: Why is Judaism answered differently from every other faith in Polemics?
Context: why Judaism is answered differe.back: It is **the faith of the people from whom Christ came**, its Scriptures are the Church's Old Testament, and **Christians have wronged Jews** for centuries.
Paul to Gentile believers: "if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but **the root thee**." With 11:29: "the gifts and calling of God are without repentance."

Context: why Judaism is answered differe.front: What does the whole disagreement with Judaism turn on?
Context: why Judaism is answered differe.back: **One man**: is Jesus of Nazareth the Messiah promised to Israel, and the Son of God? The Law, the Trinity and the Temple follow from that.

What Judaism teaches: the Thirteen Princ.back: Rabbi Moses ben Maimon of Córdoba and Egypt; wrote the *Mishneh Torah* and the *Guide for the Perplexed*; set out **Thirteen Principles** of faith (about 1168).

What Judaism teaches: the Thirteen Princ.front: Which of Maimonides' Thirteen Principles divide Jews from Christians?
What Judaism teaches: the Thirteen Princ.back: **2** (God's unity, against the Trinity), **3** (no body, against the Incarnation), **9** (the Torah unchangeable), **12** (the Messiah still to come).
About **15.8 million** (DellaPergola's 2025 core estimate), about **46 percent in Israel**; wider definitions give higher counts.

From the Temple to the rabbis: how rabbi.back: The academy where, by rabbinic tradition, **Rabbi Yohanan ben Zakkai** rebuilt Judaism around **Torah, prayer and study** after the Temple fell in **70**.
The second Jewish revolt, led by a man **Rabbi Akiva hailed as Messiah**; the Christians did not join; Jews were then banned from Jerusalem.

From the Temple to the rabbis: how rabbi.front: How did rabbinic Judaism and the Church answer the loss of the Temple differently?
From the Temple to the rabbis: how rabbi.back: Rabbis: God's presence in **Torah studied and commandments kept**; atonement by **repentance and lovingkindness**. Church: in **Christ, the temple of His body**, and His once-for-all sacrifice.

The Talmud and the Oral Torah.back: The **Mishnah**, edited by Rabbi Judah the Prince, records the oral law; the **Jerusalem** (about 400) and **Babylonian** (about 500–600) Talmuds discuss it.
The explanation of the written Torah that Orthodox Judaism holds **God gave Moses at Sinai** and teachers handed down (*Pirkei Avot* 1:1).

The Talmud and the Oral Torah.front: Why can an Orthodox Christian not answer the Talmud with "Scripture alone"?
The Talmud and the Oral Torah.back: Because the Church also holds that Scripture is read within **a tradition received with it**; the question is **which tradition is true**, the rabbis' or the apostles'.

The Septuagint and the Masoretic text: w.front: Septuagint (LXX) in the dispute with Judaism
The Septuagint and the Masoretic text: w.back: The Greek Old Testament made by **Jewish scholars in Alexandria from the 3rd century BC**; the Bible of the apostles and of the Orthodox Church.
The Hebrew text used by Jews today, fixed by about **100** and furnished with vowels by the **Masoretes** (7th–10th centuries); Aleppo Codex about 930, Leningrad Codex 1008.

The Septuagint and the Masoretic text: w.front: What do the Dead Sea Scrolls show about the Septuagint?
The Septuagint and the Masoretic text: w.back: That in Christ's time **more than one Hebrew text existed**, and that the Septuagint sometimes **translates an older Hebrew** (Deuteronomy 32:8 "sons of God"; shorter Jeremiah).

Isaiah 7:14: almah and parthenos.back: Isaiah 7:14: Hebrew *‘almah*, **"young woman"** (JPS 1917); the Septuagint translators, Jews before Christ, rendered it ***parthenos*, "virgin"**.

Isaiah 7:14: almah and parthenos.front: What is the Jewish case on Isaiah 7:14?
Isaiah 7:14: almah and parthenos.back: *‘Almah* means a young woman (*betulah* is virgin); the sign was **for King Ahaz about 735 BC**; and the Septuagint calls Dinah *parthenos* after Shechem (Genesis 34:3).

Isaiah 7:14: almah and parthenos.front: What does the disagreement over Isaiah 7:14 finally rest on?
Isaiah 7:14: almah and parthenos.back: **Whether a prophecy's meaning is limited to what its first hearers could see**, or God's word can mean more than its first fulfilment.

The Messiah: what Judaism expects and wh.back: "**Anointed one**", Greek *Christos*: in Jewish expectation a **king of David's line** who rebuilds the Temple, gathers the exiles and brings peace.

The Messiah: what Judaism expects and wh.front: What does Maimonides say the Messiah must do (Laws of Kings 11–12)?
The Messiah: what Judaism expects and wh.back: Be a **Davidic king**, bring Israel to keep the Torah, **rebuild the Temple, gather the exiles**, bring the world to serve God; if he fails or is killed, he is not the Messiah.

The Messiah: what Judaism expects and wh.front: How does the Church answer that Jesus did not do what the Messiah must do?
The Messiah: what Judaism expects and wh.back: The prophets foretell **both suffering and glory**, so **one Messiah, two comings** (Justin, Dialogue 32); the nations turning to Israel's God is his work begun.

Reading: Isaiah 52:13–53:12 in the Jewis.back: The medieval commentators (**Rashi, Ibn Ezra, Kimchi**) read the servant as **Israel**, suffering among the nations, who speak in 53:1–9.

Reading: Isaiah 52:13–53:12 in the Jewis.front: Sanhedrin 98b and the Targum on Isaiah 52:13
Reading: Isaiah 52:13–53:12 in the Jewis.back: Older Jewish texts read the passage of the **Messiah**: the Targum names the servant as the Messiah; the Talmud calls him "the leper" from 53:4.

Reading: Isaiah 52:13–53:12 in the Jewis.front: Which features of Isaiah 53 strain the reading of the servant as Israel?
Reading: Isaiah 52:13–53:12 in the Jewis.back: He is **sinless and silent**, suffers "**for the transgression of my people**", bears others' sins **in their place**, dies and then "shall see his seed".

Reading: St Justin's Dialogue with Tryph.back: The oldest surviving Christian dialogue with a Jew; Trypho, a refugee of the Bar Kokhba war, argues with Justin, reportedly at **Ephesus**.

Reading: St Justin's Dialogue with Tryph.front: What did Trypho find hardest to accept (Dialogue 89–90)?
Reading: St Justin's Dialogue with Tryph.back: Not that the Christ suffers, but that He was **crucified**, since "he that is hanged is accursed of God" (Deuteronomy 21:23).

Reading: St Justin's Dialogue with Tryph.front: How did Justin answer the scandal of the cross?
Reading: St Justin's Dialogue with Tryph.back: It was **foretold** (Isaiah 53: "reckoned among the transgressors") and **prefigured** (Moses' outstretched arms, the bronze serpent); Paul: Christ was **made a curse for us**.

Daniel's seventy weeks and the sceptre o.back: **490 years** to the anointing of "the most Holy"; an anointed one is "cut off", then **the city and sanctuary are destroyed**.
"The sceptre shall not depart from Judah ... **until Shiloh come**"; Septuagint: "he is the **expectation of nations**".

Daniel's seventy weeks and the sceptre o.front: Why do Haggai 2:9 and Malachi 3:1 matter for the time of the Messiah?
Daniel's seventy weeks and the sceptre o.back: They place the Lord's coming **to the Second Temple**, which was **destroyed in 70**: if He was to come to it, He came before then.

The Shema and the Trinity: is God one?.back: "Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one" (JPS 1917); *Shema Yisra'el, Adonai Eloheinu, Adonai echad*. Christ quotes it as the first commandment (Mark 12:29).
"**One God, the Father**, of whom are all things ... and **one Lord Jesus Christ**, by whom are all things": Paul distributes the Shema's "God" and "Lord".

The Shema and the Trinity: is God one?.front: How does the Church answer the charge that the Trinity is three gods?
The Shema and the Trinity: is God one?.back: **One essence, one will, one operation**, with the Son and Spirit eternally from the Father, the one source; each person **wholly God, not a third of God**.

The Word and the Angel of the Lord: plur.back: A figure who **speaks as God** (to Hagar, at the burning bush, Exodus 3); the Fathers read him as **the Word before the Incarnation**.
The Targums' "**Word of the LORD**" acting in the world, and **Philo of Alexandria**'s divine Logos: Jewish language of God's Word before John 1.
Study of how the rabbis condemned as heresy the view of **two divine powers**; Boyarin (2012) argued a second divine figure was at home in Second Temple Judaism.

The Law: was the Torah given for ever?.back: "I will make **a new covenant** with the house of Israel ... **Not according to the covenant** that I made with their fathers ... I will put my law in their inward parts."
The apostles and elders ruled that **Gentile believers need not be circumcised** or keep the Law of Moses.

The Law: was the Torah given for ever?.front: What does the disagreement over the Law rest on?
The Law: was the Torah given for ever?.back: Whether the ritual Law was **Israel's permanent way of life** or **preparation for the Messiah**, fulfilled when He came ("a shadow of good things to come", Hebrews 10:1).

Atonement without a Temple: repentance,.back: "So will we render for bullocks **the offering of our lips**": the rabbinic text for **prayer taking the place of sacrifice**.

Atonement without a Temple: repentance,.front: How does rabbinic Judaism hold sins are forgiven without a Temple?
Atonement without a Temple: repentance,.back: By **repentance, prayer and deeds of lovingkindness** (Yohanan ben Zakkai on Hosea 6:6), as Nineveh was spared (Jonah 3).

Atonement without a Temple: repentance,.front: How does the Church answer that repentance replaces sacrifice?
Atonement without a Temple: repentance,.back: The prophets rebuked **sacrifice without repentance**, not sacrifice; the sacrifices **pointed to the one offering** of Christ, "for it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins".

The Jewish case against Jesus, and the C.back: "No man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David": the Jewish objection to **Matthew's genealogy**, which runs through Jeconiah and Joseph.

The Jewish case against Jesus, and the C.front: How do the Fathers answer the genealogy objection?
The Jewish case against Jesus, and the C.back: **Luke's line is probably Mary's**, so Jesus is of David's blood; legal sonship through Joseph was **full sonship** in Jewish law; the curse was not on Mary's line.

The Jewish case against Jesus, and the C.front: How should the Orthodox answer the charge from Christian persecution of Jews?
The Jewish case against Jesus, and the C.back: **Grant it.** Those Christians **disobeyed Christ**, who prayed for His crucifiers; their sins are a charge against them, not against Christ.

The Church's own record toward the Jews,.back: **Eight homilies** aimed at Christians who attended synagogue, with **violent language about Jews**, later quoted by those who harmed them.
After a ritual-murder libel in the press, a mob **killed 49 Jews** in Kishinev in the Russian Empire.

The Church's own record toward the Jews,.front: How do Orthodox writers differ over Chrysostom's homilies against the Jews?
The Church's own record toward the Jews,.back: **Context first**: invective (*psogos*) of the day, aimed at Judaizing Christians (Wilken). **Plain judgement**: the words were wrong and did harm. Both: **never the Church's teaching.**

Orthodox Christians who stood with the J.front: Metropolitans Stefan of Sofia and Kiril of Plovdiv (1943)
Orthodox Christians who stood with the J.back: Led the **Bulgarian Synod's protest**; deportations from Bulgaria proper stopped and about **48,000 Jews survived**, though about 11,000 from occupied Thrace and Macedonia were killed.
Émigré nun in Paris who, with **Fr Dimitri Klepinin, Yuri Skobtsov and Ilya Fondaminsky**, hid Jews; died at **Ravensbrück, 31 March 1945**; canonised by Constantinople in **2004**.
Sent a **written protest** with leading Greeks against the deportation of the Jews of Thessaloniki and had **false baptismal certificates** issued.

Looking back: Judaism and the Church.front: What are the four points of division between Judaism and the Orthodox Church?
Looking back: Judaism and the Church.back: **The Messiah** (still to come, or Jesus), **God** (one without distinction, or Father with Word and Spirit), **the Law** (eternal, or fulfilled), **atonement** (repentance alone, or joined to Christ's sacrifice).

Looking back: Judaism and the Church.front: What does the whole disagreement with Judaism finally rest on?
Looking back: Judaism and the Church.back: **Did Israel's Scriptures foretell a Messiah who would suffer, die and rise before he reigned, and is that Messiah Jesus?**

Context: Rome, the nearest of the separa.front: Why is the Roman Catholic Church the nearest of the separated to Orthodoxy?
Context: Rome, the nearest of the separa.back: She keeps **apostolic succession, seven sacraments, the Creed, the seven councils, the Fathers, the Theotokos, the saints and icons**.

Context: Rome, the nearest of the separa.front: Which two questions have the Orthodox usually named as decisive with Rome?
Context: Rome, the nearest of the separa.back: **The filioque** (the Creed and the Trinity) and **the papacy** (authority in the Church): so St Mark of Ephesus, the 1848 Encyclical and the 1895 reply to Leo XIII.
About **1.4 billion** by her own statistics; about 18 million in the **Eastern Catholic** churches.

How the Catholic Church sees herself and.back: The one Church of Christ **"subsists in" the Catholic Church**, allowing that elements of truth and sanctification exist outside her visible structure.

How the Catholic Church sees herself and.front: How does the Catholic Church regard the Orthodox churches since Vatican II?
How the Catholic Church sees herself and.back: As having **true sacraments, priesthood and Eucharist**, as **true particular Churches** "wounded" by lacking communion with Rome; some sacramental sharing is permitted.

How the Catholic Church sees herself and.front: Why does the Orthodox Church not permit communion with Catholics in return?
How the Catholic Church sees herself and.back: Because **communion expresses a shared faith; it is not a means to reach one**, and the canons forbid sharing the Eucharist with the heterodox.

The filioque: what the Creed says and wh.front: Filioque, the Western addition to the Creed
The filioque: what the Creed says and wh.back: Latin, "**and the Son**": added in the West to the Creed's "who proceeds from the Father" (*ek tou Patros ekporeuomenon*, Constantinople 381).
Unlawful "to bring forward, or to write, or to compose a **different (ἑτέραν) Faith**" as a rival to that of Nicaea: the Orthodox canonical case against the addition.
Greek *ekporeuesthai*, to proceed **from the ultimate source**, used only of the Father; Latin has one verb, *procedere*, for that and for a broader "coming forth".

The filioque: what the Creed says and wh.front: What does the filioque dispute finally rest on?
The filioque: what the Creed says and wh.back: **Is the Father the sole source of the Spirit's existence**, or the source with the Son? And **may part of the Church change the common Creed?**

From Toledo to 1014: how \"and the Son\".back: Council of the **Visigoths' conversion from Arianism** under King Reccared; its creed as transmitted has the filioque (whether originally is debated).
Leo III **refused to add the filioque** to the Creed and set up the Creed **without it**, in Greek and Latin, on two silver shields in St Peter's.
At the coronation of **Emperor Henry II**, Pope **Benedict VIII** allowed the Creed to be sung at Mass in Rome, with the filioque.

The Latin case for the filioque: Augusti.back: The Spirit proceeds from the Father **"principally"**, and from the Son also, because **the Father gave the Son this** in begetting Him.

The Latin case for the filioque: Augusti.front: What is the Latin case for the filioque from John 16:15?
The Latin case for the filioque: Augusti.back: "**All things that the Father hath are mine**": so being a source of the Spirit is the Son's too, received from the Father, except being Father.
Defined that the Spirit proceeds from Father and Son **not as from two principles but as from one principle**, by one spiration.

St Photios and the Mystagogy: the Orthod.back: Patriarch of Constantinople 858–867 and 877–886; **Encyclical of 867** and the ***Mystagogy of the Holy Spirit*** (about 886). Feast 6 February.
"**One source**": the Father alone is **cause** (*aitia*) of the Son, by begetting, and of the Spirit, by procession.

St Photios and the Mystagogy: the Orthod.front: What is Photios's argument from the properties of the persons?
St Photios and the Mystagogy: the Orthod.back: Being the source of the Spirit is either **common** (then the Spirit causes Himself) or **personal to the Father** (then the Son cannot share it without being Father).

St Photios and the Mystagogy: the Orthod.front: What does the disagreement between Photios and the Latins rest on?
St Photios and the Mystagogy: the Orthod.back: **Is causing another person a property of the Father's person alone, or of the divine essence shared with the Son?**

\"Through the Son\": St Maximus, Gregory.back: Defended the Romans: **they do not make the Son cause of the Spirit**, knowing the Father is the one cause; they mean the Spirit comes forth **through** the Son.

\"Through the Son\": St Maximus, Gregory.front: Council of Blachernae (1285) and Gregory of Cyprus
\"Through the Son\": St Maximus, Gregory.back: The Spirit's **existence is from the Father alone**; His **eternal manifestation** (*ekphansis aidios*) is **through and from the Son**.

\"Through the Son\": St Maximus, Gregory.front: How does St Gregory Palamas speak of the Son and the Spirit?
\"Through the Son\": St Maximus, Gregory.back: The Spirit's **person is from the Father alone**; His **grace and energy** flow eternally from the Father through the Son, and even from the Son.

The filioque since 1995: clarifications,.front: The Greek and Latin Traditions regarding the Procession of the Holy Spirit (1995)
The filioque since 1995: clarifications,.back: Vatican clarification: Greek *ekporeusis* names the **Father as sole source**; Latin *procedere* is broader; the **Greek Creed of 381 is normative**.
North American Orthodox–Catholic Consultation: recommended Catholics **use the Creed without the filioque** and declare Lyons II's anathemas no longer apply.
**Pope Leo XIV and Patriarch Bartholomew** recited the Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed together **without the filioque**, for Nicaea's 1,700th anniversary.

The filioque since 1995: clarifications,.front: How do Orthodox writers differ on the gravity of the filioque?
The filioque since 1995: clarifications,.back: **Lossky, Romanides**: the root heresy of Western theology. **Bolotov (1898)**: a Western opinion wrongly made dogma, not an absolute bar. **Both**: the addition was unlawful.

Peter in the New Testament: the rock, th.back: "**Rock**": Simon's new name (John 1:42). Catholics argue that in Aramaic "Peter" and "this rock" are the same word, so **the rock is Peter**.

Peter in the New Testament: the rock, th.front: What is the Catholic case from the keys (Matthew 16:19)?
Peter in the New Testament: the rock, th.back: From Isaiah 22:22: the keys mark **the steward's office** over David's house; offices have successors; **only Peter receives the keys**.

Peter in the New Testament: the rock, th.front: What does the disagreement over Peter finally rest on?
Peter in the New Testament: the rock, th.back: **Did Christ give Peter a personal office over the other apostles that passes to the bishops of Rome alone?**

The Fathers on the rock: Origen, Cyprian.front: Origen on Matthew 16 (Commentary on Matthew XII.10)
The Fathers on the rock: Origen, Cyprian.back: Whoever confesses Christ by the Father's revelation **"becomes a Peter"**: "a rock is every disciple of Christ".

The Fathers on the rock: Origen, Cyprian.front: Cyprian, On the Unity of the Church 4–5
The Fathers on the rock: Origen, Cyprian.back: "The rest of the apostles were also the same as was Peter" ... "**The episcopate is one, each part of which is held by each one for the whole.**"
"Upon this rock": "**that is, on the faith of his confession**".
A second version of *On the Unity* 4 adding that **"primacy is given to Peter"**; Maurice Bévenot argued Cyprian wrote both.

Rome's place in the first millennium: Ig.front: Ignatius to the Romans: "presides over love"
Rome's place in the first millennium: Ig.back: The church of Rome "**presides over love**" (*prokathēmenē tēs agapēs*); Ignatius never mentions a bishop of Rome in the letter.
Acclamation after Leo's *Tome* was read, **with "Leo and Cyril taught the same thing"**: praise after examination, not acceptance without it.
Signed by Eastern bishops to end the **Acacian schism**: "in the Apostolic See the Catholic religion ... has always been kept undefiled".

The canons on the great sees: Nicaea, Co.back: Alexandria's jurisdiction over Egypt, Libya and Pentapolis, "**since the like is customary for the Bishop of Rome also**": Rome as a model of regional authority.
Old Rome's privileges were granted "**because it was the royal city**"; **equal privileges** (*isa presbeia*) to New Rome, ranking next after her. Pope Leo rejected it.
Rome cited Sardica's appeal canons as Nicene; the **African bishops found no such canons** and asked Pope Celestine not to receive appeals from Africa.

Pope Honorius: a pope condemned by an ec.back: Approved **"one will"** in Christ in letters to Sergius; **anathematised as "Honorius, the heretic"** by Constantinople III (680–681), confirmed by Leo II.

Pope Honorius: a pope condemned by an ec.front: How do Catholics answer the case of Honorius?
Pope Honorius: a pope condemned by an ec.back: His letters were **not ex cathedra**; he may have meant **no sinful will** in Christ (John IV, Maximus); Leo II condemned **negligence**, not heresy.

Pope Honorius: a pope condemned by an ec.front: What does the case of Honorius finally rest on?
Pope Honorius: a pope condemned by an ec.back: **When an ecumenical council and a pope disagree on the faith, who judges whom?**

Reading: St Gregory the Great against th.back: Pope Gregory the Great, saint of East and West (Orthodox feast **12 March**), who **refused the title "universal"** for any bishop, himself included.
"Whosoever calls himself, or desires to be called, **Universal Priest, is in his elation the precursor of Antichrist**."

Reading: St Gregory the Great against th.front: Why did Gregory say one bishop could not be "universal"?
Reading: St Gregory the Great against th.back: Because "**if one Patriarch is called Universal, the name of Patriarch in the case of the rest is derogated**": the others would cease to be truly bishops.

Reading: St Gregory the Great against th.front: How do Catholics answer Gregory on the title "universal"?
Reading: St Gregory the Great against th.back: Gregory himself wrote that **"the care and principality of the whole Church" was committed to Peter**; he refused a word, not the primacy he exercised.

From primacy to supremacy: the Dictatus.back: 27 propositions in **Gregory VII's register**: "That the Roman pontiff **alone can with right be called universal**"; "the Roman church has never erred".
Bull of **Boniface VIII** against Philip IV: both swords belong to the Church; **subjection to the Roman pontiff is necessary for salvation**.

From primacy to supremacy: the Dictatus.front: How do Catholics answer the charge that papal power changed after 1050?
From primacy to supremacy: the Dictatus.back: **Development is not corruption**: the office grew in response to need, keeping its type (Newman, *Essay on Development*, 1845); the Dictatus is not dogma.

Vatican I (1869–1870): the council and i.front: First Vatican Council (8 December 1869 – suspended 20 October 1870)
Vatican I (1869–1870): the council and i.back: Called by **Pius IX**; defined papal primacy and infallibility in ***Pastor Aeternus*** on **18 July 1870**, by **533 votes to 2**.
Bishops who thought a definition **inopportune or historically indefensible** (Hefele, Darboy, Dupanloup, Kenrick, Strossmayer); about **60 left Rome** before the final vote.
Those who rejected Vatican I, after **Döllinger** (excommunicated 1871); joined in the **Union of Utrecht** (1889).

Reading: Pastor Aeternus on the infallib.back: "From the chair": when the pope, as **pastor and teacher of all Christians**, by supreme apostolic authority, **defines a doctrine of faith or morals** to be held by the whole Church.

Reading: Pastor Aeternus on the infallib.front: Ex sese, non autem ex consensu Ecclesiae
Reading: Pastor Aeternus on the infallib.back: Papal definitions are "irreformable **of themselves, and not from the consent of the Church**": the phrase the Orthodox most deny.

Reading: Pastor Aeternus on the infallib.front: What limit does Pastor Aeternus set on papal teaching?
Reading: Pastor Aeternus on the infallib.back: "The Holy Spirit was **not promised** to the successors of Peter, that by his revelation they might make known **new doctrine**", but to guard the deposit.

Infallibility answered: the Encyclicals.front: Encyclical of the Eastern Patriarchs (1848) on who guards the faith
Infallibility answered: the Encyclicals.back: Reply of the four Eastern patriarchs to Pius IX: the guardian of the faith is **the very body of the Church, the people themselves**.
**Anthimos VII**'s reply to Leo XIII's *Praeclara gratulationis*: union only **in the faith of the seven councils**; lists Rome's innovations, papal supremacy and infallibility among them.

Infallibility answered: the Encyclicals.front: What is the Catholic reply to the Orthodox doctrine of reception?
Infallibility answered: the Encyclicals.back: **Reception cannot settle disputes at the time**; without a final arbiter the Orthodox have **no council since 787 all accept** and are divided (Moscow and Constantinople, 2018).

Infallibility answered: the Encyclicals.front: What does the disagreement over infallibility rest on?
Infallibility answered: the Encyclicals.back: **Did Christ give one visible organ that settles the faith infallibly, or the Spirit to the whole Church, known through councils and reception?**

Primacy in the Orthodox view today: Rave.back: Joint commission: **primacy and conciliarity are interdependent at every level**; Rome first in *taxis* in the first millennium. Moscow's delegation left the meeting.
Joint commission on the first millennium: primacy and synodality interdependent; Rome's place recognised, but **no authority over the East as in the West**.

Primacy in the Orthodox view today: Rave.front: How do Moscow and Constantinople differ on primacy?
Primacy in the Orthodox view today: Rave.back: **Moscow (2013)**: universal primacy is **of honour only**. **Constantinople** (Elpidophoros, "First without Equals", 2014): a **primacy with real responsibilities**.

The azymes: leavened and unleavened brea.back: **Unleavened bread** for the Eucharist, the Latin (and Armenian) use; the Greeks use **leavened** *artos*. Attacked by **Leo of Ohrid** in 1053.

The azymes: leavened and unleavened brea.front: What is the Greek case against the azymes from St John's Gospel?
The azymes: leavened and unleavened brea.back: The Last Supper was **before the Passover** (John 18:28; 19:14), so there was no unleavened bread; Christ died as the lambs were killed.

The azymes: leavened and unleavened brea.front: How do Orthodox writers differ on the azymes?
The azymes: leavened and unleavened brea.back: **Serious** (Leo of Ohrid, Niketas Stethatos; listed in 1895) or **secondary** (**Theophylact of Ohrid**: only the filioque is serious; most writers since).

1054: Humbert, Cerularius and the anathe.front: 16 July 1054: Humbert's bull on the altar of Hagia Sophia
1054: Humbert, Cerularius and the anathe.back: **Cardinal Humbert** laid a bull excommunicating **Patriarch Michael Cerularius** on the altar of Hagia Sophia; Pope Leo IX had died on **19 April 1054**.
**Paul VI and Athenagoras** regretted the acts of 1054 and declared the mutual **anathemas removed from memory**; communion was not restored.

1054: Humbert, Cerularius and the anathe.front: Why was 1054 not the break of the whole Church?
1054: Humbert, Cerularius and the anathe.back: It was between **legates of a dead pope and one patriarch**; the other patriarchs were not party; relations went on; many date the real break to **1204**.

1182 and 1204: the massacre of the Latin.back: A **Byzantine mob** killed thousands of Latins in Constantinople as Andronikos Komnenos took power; survivors were sold to the Turks.
The **Fourth Crusade** took and sacked the city for three days; a **Latin Empire** (1204–1261) and a Latin patriarch followed.

1182 and 1204: the massacre of the Latin.front: How should an Orthodox use the history of 1204?
1182 and 1204: the massacre of the Latin.back: **Neither as a trump card nor forgotten**: remember 1182 too; 1204 explains Orthodox suspicion of union, but **the doctrinal questions stand on their own terms**.

Lyons (1274): the union of an emperor.back: Pope **Gregory X**; **Michael VIII Palaiologos**'s envoys accepted the filioque and Roman primacy, for protection against **Charles of Anjou**; the Creed sung with the filioque in Greek.
The **unionist patriarch** appointed by Michael VIII; condemned by the **Council of Blachernae (1285)**.

Lyons (1274): the union of an emperor.front: Why did the union of Lyons fail?
Lyons (1274): the union of an emperor.back: It was **political**, **signed without discussion**, and **imposed by persecution**; Andronikos II repudiated it after Michael's death in 1282.

Florence (1438–1439): the union that was.back: Florence's decree of union: filioque, **both breads valid**, purgatory, and the Roman pontiff as "true vicar of Christ, and head of the whole Church".
Pope **Eugenius IV**, Emperor **John VIII**, Patriarch **Joseph II** (died in Florence, 10 June 1439); repudiated in Constantinople in **1484**.

Florence (1438–1439): the union that was.front: What does the failure of Florence finally rest on?
Florence (1438–1439): the union that was.back: **Does a council's authority come from its delegates' signatures, or from the whole Church's reception of its faith?**

St Mark of Ephesus: the one who did not.back: Mark Eugenikos, metropolitan of Ephesus from 1437; **the only Greek bishop who refused to sign** at Florence; died 23 June 1444. Feast **19 January**.
To all Orthodox: the Latins err in faith; a union that papers over differences is **a false peace**; flee communion with the unionists.

St Mark of Ephesus: the one who did not.front: How do Orthodox writers differ on St Mark's legacy for dialogue today?
St Mark of Ephesus: the one who did not.back: **A model for rejecting** the ecumenical movement (St Justin Popović, Athonite fathers) or **a model of faithful dialogue** that refuses only union without agreement in faith.

Looking back: the questions of the schis.front: What two questions does the schism with Rome finally rest on?
Looking back: the questions of the schis.back: **The Father as sole source of the Spirit**, and whether part of the Church may change the Creed; and **whether the bishop of Rome has universal jurisdiction and infallibility**.

Looking back: the questions of the schis.front: Which dates mark the schism with Rome in Polemics Stage 4?

Context: Rome after the schism, and the.front: Why do the Orthodox object to the Western doctrines defined after 1054?
Context: Rome after the schism, and the.back: Less because each is wicked than because **each was defined without the whole Church**, often on premises the East never shared (Augustine's frame of guilt and satisfaction; papal authority).
The Catholic council of the Counter-Reformation: defined original sin (1546), justification (1547), the sacraments, transubstantiation (1551), purgatory and indulgences (1563).

Created grace: what Rome holds.back: Scholastic term: a **created quality or habit** (*habitus*) produced by God in the soul, distinct from uncreated grace (God Himself, the indwelling Spirit). Aquinas, *Summa* I-II q.110.

Created grace: what Rome holds.front: Why does Aquinas hold that sanctifying grace is created?
Created grace: what Rome holds.back: Because God is **utterly simple**: if God Himself were the form of the soul we would be God by nature. So God produces in the soul a **created participation** in the divine nature.
Condemns those who say justifying grace is "only the favour of God": grace and charity are **"inherent"** in the justified.

Uncreated energies: the Orthodox answer.front: How does the Church answer the doctrine of created grace?
Uncreated energies: the Orthodox answer.back: **Grace is God Himself, given in His uncreated energies.** We share the energies, never the essence, so there is real deification without pantheism (2 Peter 1:4).
Upheld **St Gregory Palamas** against **Barlaam of Calabria**: the light of Tabor and the grace of God are **uncreated**.

Uncreated energies: the Orthodox answer.front: What does the disagreement over created grace rest on?
Uncreated energies: the Orthodox answer.back: Whether the grace that saves is **God Himself or a created effect**, and whether God's simplicity allows a real distinction of essence and energies.

The beatific vision: seeing the essence.back: Constitution of Pope **Benedict XII**: the purified souls of the saints **see the divine essence** with an intuitive, face-to-face vision.

The beatific vision: seeing the essence.front: How does the Church answer the Catholic beatific vision of the essence?
The beatific vision: seeing the essence.back: The saints see God face to face in His **uncreated light** (energies), never His **essence**. Chrysostom (*On the Incomprehensibility of God*) and Gregory of Nyssa (endless progress, "from glory to glory").

Augustine and original sin: the Western.back: Western doctrine, shaped by **St Augustine** (354–430) against **Pelagius**: Adam's sin is passed to all as a real sin; Catechism 404: "contracted", not "committed".
The Latin of Romans 5:12 Augustine read: **"in whom all sinned"**, meaning all sinned in Adam.

Augustine and original sin: the Western.front: What is Augustine's argument for original sin from infant baptism?
Augustine and original sin: the Western.back: The Church baptises infants **for the remission of sins**; infants have no personal sins; therefore they must inherit a sin. Carthage (418) taught the same.

Ancestral sin: the Orthodox reading of R.back: Greek read by most Greek Fathers as **"because"** ("because all sinned"), not the Latin **"in whom"**. The Western doctrine of inherited guilt leans on the Latin.

Ancestral sin: the Orthodox reading of R.front: How does the Church answer the doctrine of inherited guilt?
Ancestral sin: the Orthodox reading of R.back: We inherit from Adam **death, corruption and a wounded nature, not his guilt**. Death comes first and sin follows. Infants are baptised for **new life**, not acquittal. (Orthodox differ on how strongly to state the inherited condition.)
**"Ancestral sin"**: the term many Orthodox prefer to "original sin"; Romanides's 1957 dissertation bears the name.

Reading: the Council of Trent's Decree o.front: Trent, Decree on Original Sin (17 June 1546)
Reading: the Council of Trent's Decree o.back: Session V. Canon 2 condemns anyone saying Adam passed on **only death "and not sin also, which is the death of the soul"**; canon 3: sin passed on "by propagation, not by imitation".

Reading: the Council of Trent's Decree o.front: Where does Trent's canon 2 fall close to the Orthodox view?
Reading: the Council of Trent's Decree o.back: It condemns the view that Adam transmitted **only death and bodily pains**, which is near the Orthodox reading that we inherit **mortality and corruption** and sin follows from them.
Concupiscence remaining in the baptised is **not truly sin**, though Paul sometimes calls it so; aimed at Luther.

Reading: St John Chrysostom on Romans 5:.back: "He having once fallen, even they that had not eaten of the tree did from him, all of them, **become mortal**." (tr. Walker, Sheppard, Browne, rev. Stevens, NPNF 1/11, 1889).

Reading: St John Chrysostom on Romans 5:.front: What does Chrysostom say "made sinners" means in Romans 5:19?
Reading: St John Chrysostom on Romans 5:.back: **"Liable to punishment and condemned to death"**: not personally guilty, since one who is not a sinner "from his own self" would not deserve punishment.

Augustine's standing among the Orthodox:.front: How do Orthodox writers differ over St Augustine?
Augustine's standing among the Orthodox:.back: **Seraphim Rose**: a holy Father whose errors are exaggerations, to be honoured. **Romanides and Yannaras**: the root of the Western divergence, pious but not a teacher of doctrine. Both: receive a Father where he agrees with the consensus.

Augustine's standing among the Orthodox:.front: Seraphim Rose, The Place of Blessed Augustine in the Orthodox Church
Augustine's standing among the Orthodox:.back: Written **1978**, printed 1983: defends Augustine as a saint of the Church while admitting his errors on grace and the filioque.

Augustine's standing among the Orthodox:.front: Blessed Augustine in the Orthodox calendar
Augustine's standing among the Orthodox:.back: Commemorated **15 June** in many calendars, as "Blessed"; named among the Fathers by the **Fifth Ecumenical Council (553)**.

Purgatory: the Catholic case.back: Defines **that there is a purgatory** and that souls there are helped by the faithful's suffrages, chiefly the Mass; forbids "subtle questions" and "filthy lucre" in preaching. No fire, place or time defined.
The debt that may remain **after the guilt of sin is forgiven**, "to be discharged either in this world, or in the next in Purgatory".

Purgatory: the Catholic case.front: What do Catholics hold about purgatory?
Purgatory: the Catholic case.back: Those who die in grace but **not yet purified** are cleansed after death and helped by prayer; Benedict XVI (*Spe Salvi*, 2007): the fire may be **Christ Himself**.

Prayer for the dead without purgatory: t.front: How does the Church answer the doctrine of purgatory?
Prayer for the dead without purgatory: t.back: The Church **prays for the departed and believes it helps them**, by God's mercy; but denies **temporal punishment owed after forgiveness**, a purifying fire before the Judgement, and a third place.

Prayer for the dead without purgatory: t.front: What does the disagreement over purgatory rest on?
Prayer for the dead without purgatory: t.back: **After God forgives, does any penalty remain to be paid, or only healing to be given by mercy?**

Orthodox teaching (disputed among Orthodox) of demonic trials after death. Its defenders say it is a **judgement**, not satisfaction by suffering; critics such as **Archbishop Lazar Puhalo** call it allegory.

Indulgences and the treasury of merit.back: Paul VI's constitution: an indulgence is **remission of temporal punishment** for sins already forgiven, from the Church's treasury; abolished counting in days and years.
The merits of **Christ and the saints**, which the Church dispenses; defined by **Clement VI**, bull *Unigenitus* (1343).

Indulgences and the treasury of merit.front: How does the Church answer indulgences?
Indulgences and the treasury of merit.back: No debt remains after forgiveness, so nothing to remit; **no saint has surplus merit**; penance (*epitimion*) is **medicine, not payment**.

The Immaculate Conception: Ineffabilis D.back: Bull of **Pius IX** defining that Mary, from the first instant of her conception, was **preserved free from every stain of original sin** in view of Christ's merits.

The Immaculate Conception: Ineffabilis D.front: Duns Scotus and redemption by preservation
The Immaculate Conception: Ineffabilis D.back: Franciscan (about **1266–1308**): Mary was redeemed by Christ **by being preserved** from original sin, a more perfect redemption. Aquinas had held she was sanctified after conception.

The All-holy Theotokos: why the Orthodox.front: How does the Church answer the Immaculate Conception?
The All-holy Theotokos: why the Orthodox.back: She is **Panagia**, all-holy and free of personal sin; but the dogma **answers a question of inherited guilt the East does not ask**, separates her from our nature, and was defined by one bishop.

The All-holy Theotokos: why the Orthodox.front: What does the disagreement over the Immaculate Conception rest on?
The All-holy Theotokos: why the Orthodox.back: **Whether there is an inherited guilt from which she needed exemption**, and whether one bishop can define for all what the Church never defined.

The All-holy Theotokos: why the Orthodox.front: Conception of the Theotokos by St Anne (9 December)
The All-holy Theotokos: why the Orthodox.back: Orthodox feast of her conception, celebrated as the **miracle of a barren couple** answered, not as exemption from original sin.

The Assumption (1950) and the Dormition.back: **Pius XII** defined that Mary, "having completed the course of her earthly life", was **assumed body and soul** into glory; whether she died left open.
"Falling asleep": Orthodox feast of **15 August**; the Theotokos **truly died**, and was translated body and soul to heaven.

The Assumption (1950) and the Dormition.front: What does the disagreement over the Assumption rest on?
The Assumption (1950) and the Dormition.back: Not the fact but **authority**: whether a pope may make a liturgical tradition a dogma for all; and the Orthodox insist **she truly died**.

Scholasticism: Anselm, Aquinas and the m.back: **"Faith seeking understanding"**: St Anselm of Canterbury's (about 1033–1109) motto for theology.
Encyclical of **Leo XIII** making St Thomas Aquinas the model of Catholic theology and seminaries.

Scholasticism: Anselm, Aquinas and the m.front: What is the Catholic case for scholastic theology?
Scholasticism: Anselm, Aquinas and the m.back: Reason is God's gift; the Fathers (John of Damascus) also systematised; precision defends the faith against heresy.

The Orthodox critique of scholasticism,.front: How does the Church answer the scholastic method?
The Orthodox critique of scholasticism,.back: Theology flows from **prayer and the vision of the saints**, with dogma as its fence; scholasticism made it a work of concepts, and its confidence in analogy for God's essence underlies created grace and the beatific vision of the essence.
In *Ways of Russian Theology* (**1937**), Fr Georges Florovsky's name for Orthodox theology taught from **Latin** textbooks from the 17th century; answered by the neo-patristic synthesis.

Byzantine admirers of Aquinas: **Kydones** (about 1324–1398) translated the *Summa contra Gentiles* into Greek; **Scholarios** (about 1400–1473), first patriarch after 1453, admired Aquinas while rejecting the filioque.

Satisfaction and merit: Anselm's atoneme.back: St Anselm's "Why God Became Man": sin dishonours God; only the **God-man** can make **satisfaction**; Christ's free death is an infinite gift.

Satisfaction and merit: Anselm's atoneme.front: How do Orthodox writers differ over satisfaction language?
Satisfaction and merit: Anselm's atoneme.back: **Antony Khrapovitsky** (*The Dogma of Redemption*, 1917), Romanides and others reject it as juridical; **St Philaret's Catechism**, Dositheus and the manuals use it. All refuse to make one theory the account.

The sacraments: seven, valid, and ex ope.back: "From the work worked": Trent, Session VII (1547), canon 8: sacraments give grace **by the rite itself**, not by the minister's holiness.

The sacraments: seven, valid, and ex ope.front: What does the disagreement over sacraments outside the Church rest on?
The sacraments: seven, valid, and ex ope.back: Augustine: a sacrament is **valid by its rite** wherever performed. Cyprian and the Orthodox: the mysteries **belong to the one Church** and cannot be separated from her.

The sacraments: seven, valid, and ex ope.front: How do Orthodox writers differ over receiving Catholics?
The sacraments: seven, valid, and ex ope.back: **Akriveia**: Nikodemos's *Pedalion* (1800), the decree of **1755**, Peter Heers: baptise; chrismation is economy only. **Oikonomia**: Russia since 1667 and most churches receive by confession or chrismation.

Baptism, chrismation and communion: why.back: Decree under **Pius X** setting first communion in the Latin Church at the **age of reason** (about seven).

Baptism, chrismation and communion: why.front: Why did Latin confirmation become separate from baptism?
Baptism, chrismation and communion: why.back: In the West only the **bishop** confirms; as dioceses grew it waited for his visit. In the East the **priest** chrismates with myron the bishop consecrated, so the rite never split.

Baptism, chrismation and communion: why.front: How does the Church answer delayed infant communion?
Baptism, chrismation and communion: why.back: Initiation is **one mystery**; St Cyprian (*On the Lapsed*) shows infants communed; if an infant may be baptised without understanding, he may be fed.

The Eucharist: transubstantiation and th.back: The **whole substance** of bread and wine changes into Christ's Body and Blood while the **species** (appearances) remain.
Orthodox word for the **change** of the gifts; the **epiclesis** is the invocation of the Holy Spirit "upon these gifts". Cabasilas defended it against the Latins.

The Eucharist: transubstantiation and th.front: How do Orthodox writers differ over the word metousiosis?
The Eucharist: transubstantiation and th.back: **Dositheus (1672)** and **Mogila (1640)** used it (transubstantiation); others, with Khomiakov and many modern theologians, call it a Latin borrowing. All agree on the reality of the change.

The Unia: the Union of Brest (1595–96) a.back: Metropolitan **Michael Rohoza** of Kiev and other bishops accepted union with Rome; proclaimed at **Brest, October 1596**, while an Orthodox counter-synod (Prince Konstantin Ostrozky) condemned it.

The Unia: the Union of Brest (1595–96) a.front: How does the Church answer the Unia?
The Unia: the Union of Brest (1595–96) a.back: Union was made by **bishops without their flocks**, enforced by the Polish state, and treated Orthodox as a **mission field**; the Orthodox hierarchy was restored only in **1620** by Patriarch Theophanes of Jerusalem.
Greek Catholic archbishop of Polotsk who pressed the union and seized Orthodox churches; **killed by an Orthodox mob in Vitebsk**. Catholics venerate him as a martyr.

The Unia from both sides: Lviv 1946, Bal.back: Soviet-organised gathering, with **no Greek Catholic bishop**, that annulled the Union of Brest and gave the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church to the Moscow Patriarchate.
Joint Orthodox–Catholic text: **uniatism is not a method or model** of unity; Eastern Catholics have the right to exist; neither side should proselytise the other.

The Unia from both sides: Lviv 1946, Bal.front: What does the disagreement over the Unia rest on?
The Unia from both sides: Lviv 1946, Bal.back: Whether union may be made by **a part of a church** with Rome, or only by **the whole Church with the whole Church**.

Vatican II and the lifting of the anathe.back: Vatican II's decree on ecumenism: the Eastern churches have **true sacraments**, priesthood and Eucharist; their traditions are often **complementary** to the West's.
**Paul VI** and **Patriarch Athenagoras I** "removed from memory" the excommunications of 1054; communion was not restored.

Vatican II and the lifting of the anathe.front: How do Orthodox writers differ over ecumenical dialogue with Rome?
Vatican II and the lifting of the anathe.back: **For**: Athenagoras, Bartholomew, Zizioulas, the Council of Crete (2016): love requires meeting. **Against or wary**: **St Justin Popović**, *The Orthodox Church and Ecumenism* (1974), many Athonites: love tells the truth.

The dialogue today: Ravenna, Chieti, Ale.back: Joint Commission text on conciliarity and authority: a "first" at local, regional and universal levels; agreement that Rome was first in the first millennium, **disagreement on what that meant**.
Pope **Leo XIV** and Patriarch **Bartholomew** prayed at Nicaea for the **1,700th anniversary** and signed a joint declaration at the Phanar urging a **common Easter**.
At **Pannonhalma**, the coordinating committee judged its draft on infallibility needed more revision; next meeting planned for **June 2027** (as of November 2026).

What a Catholic says back: the strongest.front: Newman, Essay on the Development of Christian Doctrine (1845)
What a Catholic says back: the strongest.back: Argued that true doctrine **grows like a seed**: later dogmas are in the deposit as the oak in the acorn.

What a Catholic says back: the strongest.front: How does the Church answer the argument from development of doctrine?
What a Catholic says back: the strongest.back: The faith is "once delivered" (Jude 3); words are found by **councils of the whole Church** to express what was always believed (Vincent of Lérins). A development defined by one part against the other's tradition is innovation.
John Paul II's encyclical: the Church should breathe with **"both lungs"**; invited the Orthodox to help find a way of exercising the papacy both could accept.

Looking back: the questions since the sc.front: What two premises underlie most post-schism disputes with Rome?
Looking back: the questions since the sc.back: **Augustine's frame** of guilt, satisfaction and merit (original sin, purgatory, indulgences, the Immaculate Conception), and **the authority to define** (the papacy).

Looking back: the questions since the sc.front: How should an Orthodox name the premise in a conversation with a Catholic?
Looking back: the questions since the sc.back: Plainly: "We don't think guilt is inherited", or "We don't think one bishop can define for all": that is where the conversation will end up.

Context: the Reformation, and why the Or.front: The five solas of the Reformation
Context: the Reformation, and why the Or.back: *Sola scriptura*, *sola fide*, *sola gratia*, *solus Christus*, *soli Deo gloria*: Scripture, faith, grace, Christ and God's glory **alone**; a later summary of the Reformers' teaching.

Context: the Reformation, and why the Or.front: Why does the Orthodox answer to the Reformation differ from Rome's?
Context: the Reformation, and why the Or.back: Rome answered **inside the Western frame** of merit, satisfaction and papal authority. The Orthodox stand outside it: salvation is **union with God**, in which faith and works are both the life of grace.

Luther and the Ninety-five Theses (1517).back: Martin Luther's (1483–1546) theses against **Tetzel's indulgence preaching**. Thesis 1: Christ "willed that the whole life of believers should be repentance".
Bull of **Leo X** condemning 41 of Luther's propositions; Luther burned it; excommunicated January 1521, then refused to recant at the **Diet of Worms** (April 1521).

Luther and the Ninety-five Theses (1517).front: How does the Church read Luther's protest of 1517?
Luther and the Ninety-five Theses (1517).back: Thesis 1 the Orthodox can sign; Tetzel's indulgences and the treasury were a **Western problem** the East never had. The question is what Luther put in their place.

Sola scriptura: the Protestant case.back: **"By Scripture alone"**: Scripture is the **only infallible rule of faith**, judging every council and Father. Distinguished by careful Protestants from *solo* or *nuda scriptura* (Scripture without creeds).
The whole counsel of God is "expressly set down in Scripture, or by good and necessary consequence may be deduced from Scripture", nothing to be added by "traditions of men".

Sola scriptura: the Protestant case.front: What do Protestants hold about Scripture and tradition?
Sola scriptura: the Protestant case.back: Scripture is God-breathed; Christ judged tradition by it (Mark 7:13); councils have erred (Article 21); the Fathers appealed to Scripture; what is necessary is **clear** to the unlearned.

Scripture in the Church: the Orthodox an.front: How does the Church answer sola scriptura?
Scripture in the Church: the Orthodox an.back: Scripture does not teach it; the **Church preceded and canonised** the New Testament; every heretic quotes Scripture (Irenaeus's mosaic); the Fathers read Scripture **within the Church's faith**.

Scripture in the Church: the Orthodox an.front: What does the disagreement over sola scriptura rest on?
Scripture in the Church: the Orthodox an.back: **Whether the final rule is the text read by each believer, or the text as the Spirit-led Church has always read it.**

Scripture in the Church: the Orthodox an.front: Irenaeus's mosaic of the king (Against Heresies 1.8.1)
Scripture in the Church: the Orthodox an.back: Heretics rearrange the stones of a mosaic of a king into a **dog or fox**: the stones are Scripture, the pattern is the Church's faith.

The canon: the deuterocanonical books an.back: Septuagint books outside the Hebrew canon (Wisdom, Sirach, Tobit, Judith, Maccabees and others). **Protestants**: "Apocrypha" (Article 6; Westminster 1.3). **Orthodox**: read as Scripture.
In his 1522 New Testament preface Luther called **James** "an epistle of straw" beside the chief books, and placed Hebrews, James, Jude and Revelation at the end.

The canon: the deuterocanonical books an.front: How do Orthodox writers differ over the deuterocanonical books?
